questions.prompt: Which statement best describes your ability to explain where total technology spend goes?
questions.intent: Assess whether the CIO has an enterprise-wide cost baseline rather than fragmented views.
questions.answerDesign: Choose the statement that best reflects the normal enterprise reality.

options.label: We have an enterprise-wide view with major technology categories reconciled and ownership clear.
We have a strong IT view, but some business-led or indirect technology spend sits outside it.
We know the major categories, but allocation and ownership are inconsistent.
We mainly see vendor or departmental spend and cannot reliably build an enterprise picture.
We do not have a reliable enterprise technology spend baseline.

questions.prompt: How effectively does your organization optimize cloud consumption against actual business demand?
questions.intent: Determine whether cloud consumption is actively managed for waste, sizing and demand alignment.
questions.answerDesign: Use the position that best represents current practice, not future ambition.

questions.prompt: For major technology investments, how consistently do you measure the business outcome you expected to achieve?
questions.intent: Assess whether major technology investments are linked to measurable business outcomes.
questions.answerDesign: Choose the statement that best describes the normal practice, not an exceptional program.

options.label: We define a quantified baseline and target before approval, then track the outcome after delivery.
We define business KPIs and review them after delivery for major investments.
We track delivery, usage, or adoption metrics, but not consistently the business outcome.
Measurement varies by investment and is not applied consistently.
We do not consistently measure whether expected business benefits were achieved.

findings.title: Technology spend baseline is not sufficiently transparent
findings.description: The current cost view may not provide a reliable enterprise picture for challenge, allocation or investment decisions.

findings.title: Technology investment benefits are not consistently measured
findings.description: Benefits may be tracked unevenly, reducing the CIO's ability to distinguish investment that creates value from investment that simply consumes budget.

findings.title: Cloud consumption may contain avoidable leakage
findings.description: Cloud consumption appears insufficiently aligned to actual demand, creating potential optimization and cost-avoidance opportunity subject to evidence validation.

recommendations.title: Establish an Enterprise Technology Spend Baseline
recommendations.description: Create a reconciled view of technology spend across major categories, ownership and material business-led spend.

recommendations.title: Run a Cloud Economics Diagnostic
recommendations.description: Validate demand alignment, rightsizing, commitment strategy, tagging and consumption governance before sizing any savings opportunity.

recommendations.title: Institutionalize Benefits Realization
recommendations.description: Set measurable benefit baselines, targets and post-implementation reviews for major technology investments.

settings.opportunityLabel: Illustrative opportunity range — requires evidence validation
